This paper addresses visual speech recognition (VSR) by proposing a method to handle head-pose variation through adaptive feature modulation. The core contribution involves computer vision techniques for analyzing visual speech from video, specifically dealing with appearance transformations caused by pose variation. The work focuses on image/video analysis and visual recognition tasks, which are central to computer vision research.

This paper focuses on interpreting and understanding how Vision Transformers (ViTs) represent visual concepts internally through concept circuits. The core contribution involves analyzing visual representations, concept interactions, and model interpretability for computer vision models. While the paper touches on model behavior analysis, the primary emphasis is on vision model interpretation, concept discovery in visual domains, and applications to vision tasks like spurious correlation detection in visual datasets (Waterbird dataset).

This paper introduces a benchmark dataset for tracking points across multiple camera views in 3D space. The core contribution is a multi-view point tracking benchmark with sequences, calibrated cameras, and annotated trajectories. The paper focuses on visual tracking, 3D reconstruction from multiple views, and point correspondence - all central topics in computer vision. While it has applications in robotics and autonomous driving, the primary technical contribution is a computer vision benchmark for multi-view point tracking and 3D geometry recovery.

This paper focuses on image difference captioning, which involves analyzing visual content from image pairs and generating natural language descriptions of changes. The core contributions include a benchmark dataset with captions and spatial masks for image pairs, evaluation protocols for assessing captioning ability, and benchmarking of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The primary task is grounded image difference captioning - generating natural language descriptions of visual changes - which falls squarely within computer vision and pattern recognition.

This paper addresses semantic segmentation, which is a core computer vision task involving 'image and video analysis, visual recognition' as stated in the cs.CV definition. The work focuses on 'class-incremental semantic segmentation' with 'image-level supervision' and uses 'diffusion-based generative replay' to generate replay data for segmentation models. While the paper involves continual learning concepts, the primary contribution is solving a segmentation problem (a visual recognition task) using generative methods.

This paper proposes a method for learning 2D visual representations using contrastive learning enhanced with depth information for 3D spatial awareness. The core contribution involves image and visual representation learning through contrastive objectives applied to 2D pixels with 3D spatial guidance. The work focuses on visual representation learning, image understanding, and the integration of depth cues into contrastive frameworks, which are central topics in computer vision.

This paper addresses RGB-T (RGB and thermal) salient object detection, which is fundamentally a computer vision task involving image analysis and visual recognition. The core contributions involve image fusion techniques, feature extraction from visual data, and object detection/segmentation - all central to computer vision. The paper proposes modules for cross-modal fusion of RGB and thermal images to identify salient objects, which is explicitly a vision problem rather than language processing, security, robotics, databases, software engineering, HCI, or distributed computing.

This paper addresses security architecture in automotive networks, specifically focusing on Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) implementation through cryptographic protocols (MACsec/MKA), key management, and network access control. The core contribution involves cryptographic authentication, access revocation, key rotation, and security policy enforcement in automotive systems. While it discusses SDN (Software-Defined Networking) as a management mechanism, the primary focus is on cryptographic security, authentication mechanisms, and security architecture rather than distributed systems or networking infrastructure.

This paper investigates the capabilities and limitations of large language model (LLM) agents applied to penetration testing tasks. The core focus is on security vulnerabilities and attack capabilities of AI systems, specifically examining 'what they can do or how they fail' in offensive security contexts. The paper's primary contribution is analyzing security implications and defensive measurements against LLM-based penetration testing agents, which falls squarely within cryptography and security research.

This paper focuses on side-channel attacks against chip security, specifically exploiting clock freezing through cryogenic temperature exposure to extract sensitive information. The work involves hardware security vulnerabilities, attack implementations on FPGAs/SoCs, and countermeasures against these attacks. The core contribution is demonstrating a physical attack vector that bypasses security sensors and defenses in cryptographic hardware.

This paper focuses on identifying mislabeled apps in a dataset used for training a Google Play app removal prediction model. The core contribution involves applying label noise detection methods (Isolation Forest, Neighborhood Disagreement, Prediction Inconsistency) to identify suspected mislabeled instances in a dataset of 870,514 apps. The work is fundamentally about data quality, machine learning model training, and empirical evaluation of detection methods on a real-world dataset. While it involves some security aspects (spam detection, malware checking via VirusTotal), the primary focus is on the machine learning and data management problem of label noise detection rather than security itself.

This paper presents Codetta, a steganographic protocol for hiding covert communication between multi-agent LLM systems. The core contribution involves cryptographic techniques (steganography, key exchange, error-correcting codes) to enable undetectable collusion in multi-agent systems. While the paper involves LLMs and natural language, the primary focus is on cryptographic security, steganographic protocols, and adversarial attacks/defenses rather than NLP tasks or language understanding.

This paper presents Odin, an FHE (Fully Homomorphic Encryption) inference system for privacy-preserving LLM inference. The core contribution is optimizing ciphertext packing and model execution for encrypted computation. While the paper involves LLMs (which might suggest cs.CL), the primary focus is on cryptographic techniques for privacy-preserving computation - specifically designing and optimizing FHE schemes (CKKS-based) for efficient encrypted inference. The technical contributions center on cryptographic packing schemes, homomorphic operations, and encryption-aware system design rather than on language model architectures or NLP tasks.

This paper investigates how autonomous agents lose control during task execution, examining factors like goal pressure, control degradation, and unsafe opportunities. The core focus is on agent behavior, safety constraints, and decision-making in multi-turn environments. While it touches on security concerns (loss of control, unauthorized execution), the primary contribution is understanding agent behavior and control mechanisms rather than cryptographic or security protocols. The work is fundamentally about autonomous agent systems and their behavioral properties.

This paper focuses on transaction validation, UTXO (Unspent Transaction Output) workflows, and ledger extension mechanisms. The core contribution involves formal methods for validating multi-step transactions using recursive invariants, with emphasis on validation logic, transaction structure, and ledger consistency. While blockchain-related, the paper's primary concern is the formal specification and validation of transaction workflows rather than cryptographic security, distributed consensus, or system architecture. The work presents a DSL, formal semantics, and validation algorithms for transaction processing, which aligns most closely with database transaction management and query processing concepts, though it could tangentially relate to distributed systems.

This paper focuses on network-based intrusion detection, specifically designing and evaluating a system that combines Suricata (a network intrusion detection tool) with machine learning (Random Forest) for detecting network attacks. The core contribution involves network security, attack detection, and system evaluation rather than natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, databases, software engineering practices, human-computer interaction, or distributed computing infrastructure.

This paper presents Attestream, a blockchain-based system for managing machine learning data streams with verifiable lifecycle provenance and usage tracking. The core contributions involve cryptographic verification, smart contracts (Solidity), digital signatures (EIP-712), and security mechanisms for data leakage attribution. While the paper deals with ML data streams, the primary technical focus is on cryptographic protocols, blockchain security, and authentication mechanisms rather than on machine learning algorithms or computer vision tasks.

This paper presents a graph-based framework for security analysis of O-RAN systems, focusing on building a queryable database of security threats, vulnerabilities, and relationships. The core contribution is a security analysis tool and methodology, which falls under cryptography and security research. While the paper involves database design and LLM-assisted data extraction, the primary focus is on security assessment, threat modeling, and vulnerability analysis of a telecommunications infrastructure.

This paper focuses on detecting mismatches between natural language descriptions and code execution in DAO governance systems. The core contribution involves using large language models (LLMs) to map textual descriptions to execution traces and identify deceptive proposals. The work is fundamentally about natural language processing and understanding - specifically, comparing free-form natural language descriptions with structured execution behavior to detect attacks. While it involves blockchain/smart contracts, the primary technical challenge and contribution is in the NLP domain (evidence mapping, LLM-based analysis, text-to-code understanding).

This paper presents GlitchLab, a hardware-in-the-loop platform for physical fault injection attacks targeting security vulnerabilities. The core focus is on cryptographic security (AES key recovery), authentication bypass, and control flow attacks through hardware fault injection. The work addresses security vulnerabilities and attack methodologies, which are central topics in cryptography and security research.

This paper focuses on security evaluation and risk assessment of language model agent skills, presenting a library system for analyzing attack traces and security vulnerabilities. The core contribution involves creating a searchable database of security cases, analyzing attack trajectories, and improving security guards for agent systems. While it involves language models and agents, the primary emphasis is on security analysis, vulnerability documentation, and cryptographic/security evaluation methodologies rather than on natural language processing techniques or model capabilities themselves.

This paper focuses on security vulnerabilities in LLM-based multi-agent systems, specifically examining how deceptive worker agent descriptions can be injected to mislead the planner component. The core contribution involves identifying attack vectors through 'registration-time injection,' analyzing real-world agent descriptions, constructing attack strategies, and proposing a defense mechanism (DescGuard). The work is fundamentally about security threats, vulnerabilities, and defenses in distributed multi-agent systems.

This paper presents a security attack against privacy-preserving LLM systems, specifically targeting embedding obfuscation schemes. The core contribution is a novel attack method (Proxy Manifold Alignment) that breaks the security of Embedding-to-Embedding Obfuscation (E2EO) schemes. The paper focuses on cryptographic vulnerabilities, attack mechanisms, and privacy breaches in LLM systems, which are central topics in cryptography and security research.

This paper addresses security vulnerabilities in homomorphic encryption-based large language model inference, specifically focusing on jailbreak attacks and proposing guardrail mechanisms that operate on encrypted data. The core contribution involves cryptographic techniques (homomorphic encryption) applied to secure LLM inference and adversarial attack detection. While it involves LLMs, the primary focus is on cryptographic security properties and encrypted computation rather than language processing itself.

This paper focuses on cybersecurity alert fatigue in security operations centers (SOCs), proposing and evaluating risk-based alerting (RBA) as a mitigation strategy. The core contribution involves systematic evaluation of alert prioritization methods, security threat detection, and defense mechanisms against false alerts. The work is fundamentally about cryptography, security, and defense strategies in cybersecurity contexts.

This paper focuses on stegomalware embedded in large language model weights, examining both attack and defense mechanisms using permutation symmetries. The core contribution involves security threats and countermeasures for LLMs, which falls squarely within cryptography and security research. While the paper involves LLMs (which could suggest cs.CL), the primary focus is on embedding malicious payloads, defending against such attacks, and analyzing security vulnerabilities—all central concerns of cs.CR.

This paper focuses on privacy risks and security vulnerabilities in dot map visualizations, specifically analyzing how location information can be recovered from published maps through exploitation of rendering artifacts. The core contribution is a privacy attack framework (AutoLocate) and mitigation strategies. This falls squarely within cryptography and security research, which encompasses 'attacks and defenses, privacy' as stated in the cs.CR definition.

This paper focuses on using Wi-Fi signal data (RSSI and CSI) for human localization and position prediction. The core contribution involves cross-domain inference where RSSI data is fed into CSI-trained models to predict human locations within a room. The work is fundamentally about signal processing and localization techniques rather than natural language, vision, cryptography, robotics, databases, software engineering, user interaction, or distributed systems. The privacy implications mentioned are secondary to the primary technical contribution of demonstrating feasibility of Wi-Fi-based indoor localization.

This paper presents AgentDrift, a benchmark dataset for detecting prompt injection attacks in LLM agent trajectories. The core contribution is a labeled corpus of tool-call sequences with step-by-step annotations for security analysis. While it involves LLM agents and natural language processing elements, the primary focus is on security vulnerabilities (prompt injection attacks), detection mechanisms, and the creation of a labeled benchmark for evaluating security defenses. The paper's main contribution is a security-focused benchmark rather than advances in NLP, computer vision, or other domains.

This paper addresses security vulnerabilities in large language models, specifically focusing on defending against white-box editing jailbreaks through representation engineering attacks. The core contribution is a defense mechanism called 'Bait-and-Recover' that involves weight-level modifications and poisoning internal signals to prevent attackers from suppressing safety alignment. The work is fundamentally about cryptographic and security aspects of machine learning systems, including attack and defense mechanisms.

This paper focuses on smartphone splash ads, their characterization, and evaluation of countermeasures/defenses against them. The work involves analyzing advertising implementations, testing defensive tools, examining user interface interactions, and accessibility issues. While it touches on security aspects (defenses against unwanted behavior), the primary focus is on characterizing a specific mobile app phenomenon and evaluating existing countermeasures from a user perspective, which aligns most closely with Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) - specifically user interface issues, accessibility concerns, and user-facing defensive mechanisms.

This paper presents Enc53, a protocol for authenticated DNS encryption that addresses cryptographic security and authentication challenges in the DNS infrastructure. The work focuses on DNSSEC authentication, TLS-based encryption, post-quantum cryptographic primitives (ML-DSA, FN-DSA-512), and secure communication protocols. While it involves DNS (a network protocol), the primary contribution is cryptographic: designing stateless session tickets anchored in DNSSEC and implementing authenticated encryption for DNS queries using post-quantum algorithms.

This paper addresses privacy vulnerabilities in federated learning systems, specifically focusing on client identity inference attacks and defenses using differential privacy and cryptographic techniques. The core contributions involve analyzing gradient-based attacks, proposing privacy-preserving defenses (noise addition, clipping, ensemble methods), and providing formal privacy guarantees through differential privacy accounting. While the application domain is vehicular networks, the primary technical focus is on privacy and security aspects of federated learning systems rather than vehicle control, robotics, or computer vision.

This paper addresses cyberattack detection in network traffic using concept drift mitigation techniques. The core contribution involves feature selection and stability analysis for intrusion detection, with evaluation on network traffic datasets. While the paper touches on security aspects (cyberattacks, intrusion detection), its primary focus is on machine learning methodology for handling concept drift in network traffic analysis, making it fundamentally a security/cryptography paper rather than a general ML paper.

This paper introduces a novel vulnerability analysis paradigm for detecting indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities in MCP servers using only metadata, without system access or runtime interaction. The core contribution is a security analysis method (MCPSEC) that identifies vulnerabilities in closed-source systems. This work is fundamentally about cryptography, security vulnerabilities, detection methods, and attack analysis, which are central topics in the cs.CR (Cryptography and Security) category.

This paper addresses privacy concerns in deploying large language models with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems using Differential Privacy (DP). The core contribution involves managing privacy budgets in LLM applications, which falls under natural language processing and computational linguistics. The paper discusses LLMs, retrieval mechanisms, and generation strategies - all central to NLP. While it touches on privacy (cs.CR), the primary focus is on improving LLM performance with privacy constraints rather than cryptography or security mechanisms themselves.

This paper addresses security vulnerabilities in third-party adapters for language models, specifically focusing on detecting and preventing backdoors through cryptographic verification and zero-knowledge proofs. The core contribution is a supply-chain security primitive called ServeGuard that verifies adapters cannot hide malicious channels. The work involves cryptography (zero-knowledge proofs, verification), security (backdoor detection, confinement), and language models, but the primary focus is on cryptographic verification and security guarantees rather than language processing itself.

The paper describes MimicSat, a testbed system designed for cybersecurity research on satellite systems, with emphasis on 'controlled spacecraft cybersecurity studies involving attacks, faults, and defensive responses.' While it involves cyber-physical systems and satellite operations, the primary focus is on cybersecurity research, attack scenarios, and defensive mechanisms. The paper's core contribution is providing an experimental environment for security studies rather than addressing computer vision, databases, software engineering practices, or other alternative categories.

This paper focuses on analyzing infostealer malware, its victims, and the security implications of credential theft and data breaches. The core contribution involves studying malware attacks, security vulnerabilities, victim compromise patterns, and building a dataset for security research. The paper explicitly addresses cryptography, authentication, attacks, defenses, and privacy concerns - all central topics in cybersecurity research. While it involves data analysis, the primary focus is on security threats, malware analysis, and attack patterns rather than database management or general data science.

This paper focuses on detecting attacks in blockchain applications by analyzing transaction call traces and function name sequences using machine learning (transformers). The core contribution involves developing an automated detection framework (TxLucent) that identifies malicious transactions without requiring source code or handcrafted rules. While blockchain is the application domain, the primary technical contribution is in security detection methodology, making this fundamentally a cryptography and security paper rather than a systems or database paper.

This paper focuses on differential privacy techniques applied to EEG data anonymization in clinical settings. While it involves EEG signal processing and machine learning evaluation, the primary contribution is addressing privacy protection through cryptographic and privacy-preserving methods (differential privacy, perturbation mechanisms). The core technical contribution centers on privacy-utility trade-offs using formal privacy guarantees, which is characteristic of cryptography and security research rather than signal processing or clinical applications.

This paper evaluates safety mechanisms in language models by testing how well they refuse harmful requests, particularly when those requests are encoded or obfuscated. The core contribution involves analyzing model behavior on both harmful and benign prompts under various transformations, measuring refusal rates and 'harm gaps' across different models and training pipelines. The work is fundamentally about security vulnerabilities in AI systems and how to properly evaluate them.

This paper focuses on evaluating backdoor repair methods in machine learning models, specifically addressing how to measure the preservation of benign performance after removing backdoor attacks. The core contribution involves security evaluation metrics for detecting and measuring degradation in model performance, which falls squarely within cryptography and security research. The paper discusses attack success rates, defense mechanisms, and security vulnerabilities in neural networks.

This paper focuses on verifying cryptographic software implementations, specifically targeting the verification of cryptographic algorithms (SHA-3, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, HPKE) and their correctness properties. The core contribution involves developing methodology and tooling for formal verification of cryptographic code using Lean and Rust. While the paper involves software engineering aspects (verification, testing), the primary domain is cryptography and security verification.

This paper focuses on security vulnerabilities in DRAM systems (RowHammer attacks and countermeasures) and their impact on real-time system timing behavior. The core contribution is demonstrating how security countermeasures can be exploited to break timing guarantees in safety-critical systems. While it touches on real-time systems and WCET analysis, the primary focus is on cryptographic/security vulnerabilities, attacks, and defenses against hardware-level threats (RowHammer). The paper is fundamentally about security exploitation and defense mechanisms.

This paper is a security-focused empirical study examining whether AI coding assistants verify trust signals (software bills of materials, signed releases, build provenance attestations) before installing software packages. The core contribution involves auditing the behavior of AI systems in the software supply chain context, measuring verification practices, and analyzing security vulnerabilities. While it touches on software engineering practices and supply chain security, the primary focus is on cryptographic trust signals, verification mechanisms, and security vulnerabilities in the AI-assisted software installation process.

This paper focuses on designing and evaluating a system for incident response and orchestration in information systems. The core contributions involve system architecture, rule engines, workflow management, and integration of LLMs into a controlled operational system. While it touches on NLP (using an LLM), the primary emphasis is on system design, incident management workflows, and operational reliability rather than language processing itself. This aligns most closely with cs.SE (Software Engineering) as it addresses system design, testing, verification, and operational tooling for incident response systems.

This paper focuses on adversarial attacks and defenses for machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). The core contributions involve evaluating adversarial evasion attacks, defense strategies, and proposing detection methods for adversarial samples in the context of network security. While it involves machine learning, the primary emphasis is on cryptography, security, and adversarial robustness rather than language processing, computer vision, robotics, databases, software engineering, human-computer interaction, or distributed computing.

This paper focuses on security vulnerabilities in mixed-signal integrated circuits, specifically demonstrating how analog input pins can be exploited as covert exfiltration channels through hardware trojan attacks. The work involves cryptographic/security analysis of hardware vulnerabilities, attack mechanisms, and defense considerations in semiconductor devices.

This paper focuses on measuring and analyzing security vulnerabilities in software supply chains, including dependency management, vulnerability propagation, and Software Composition Analysis (SCA) tools. The core contribution is a research agenda for quantitative security measurement and analysis of software ecosystems. While it touches on software development practices, the primary emphasis is on security assessment, vulnerability management, and cryptographic/security aspects of software dependencies rather than general software engineering practices.

This paper focuses on security vulnerabilities and protection mechanisms in Agent-Integrated Software systems where human operations and agent actions coexist. The core contribution is analyzing security problems (context misuse, authorization violation, execution control, effect integrity) and proposing a framework for security analysis. This is fundamentally a security and cryptography paper addressing authentication, access control, and policy enforcement in software systems.

This paper focuses on detecting security vulnerabilities (logic flaws) in blockchain-enabled IoT systems by analyzing smart contracts and device firmware. The core contribution involves developing a machine learning framework (multi-agent heterogeneous graph attention) for vulnerability detection across different system layers. While it touches on cryptography and security concerns, the primary emphasis is on security vulnerability detection methodology and the technical approach to identifying flaws, which falls under cryptography and security research.

This paper presents a dataset of smart contract vulnerabilities from the CVE database, focusing on Ethereum smart contracts with source code, bytecode, and vulnerability labels. The work involves security vulnerability analysis, classification, and localization in blockchain programs. The primary focus is on cryptographic security vulnerabilities and their documentation in smart contracts, making this a security-focused contribution rather than one primarily about language processing, vision, robotics, databases, software engineering practices, human-computer interaction, or distributed systems.

This paper focuses on verifiable delay functions (VDFs), cryptographic protocols for attestation, and security analysis of a protocol composition called Fresh-Challenge VDF Attestations. The core contribution involves cryptographic primitives, security assumptions, and protocol design for establishing evidence about computational latency. The paper explicitly states it is not proposing new VDF constructions but rather a protocol/design analysis layer with security properties under cryptographic assumptions.

This paper presents CONCURDEP, a static analysis tool for detecting concurrency-related bugs in CPython, specifically focusing on dependency invalidation when the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is removed. The work involves source-level static analysis, program verification, and bug detection in software systems. The core contribution is a static analysis technique with plugins and evaluation on production code, which aligns with software engineering research focused on verification, testing, and tooling of software systems.

This paper focuses on jailbreak attacks against large language models, specifically cipher-based attacks that bypass model alignment and safety measures. The core contribution involves demonstrating how LLMs can learn covert communication schemes through prompting and in-context learning to circumvent safety mechanisms. This is fundamentally about security vulnerabilities in language models and adversarial attacks against them, which falls squarely within cryptography and security research.

This paper addresses model misappropriation and identity verification of AI models through a challenge-response framework. The core contribution is a security mechanism for verifying whether a deployed AI model matches a claimed identity, which falls under cryptography and security concerns. While the paper uses image classifiers as a case study, the primary focus is on authentication, verification protocols, and defending against model theft—all central to cs.CR rather than cs.CV.

This paper focuses on humanoid robot control and motion tracking, specifically developing a policy learning framework for sparse timed keyframe motion tracking on humanoid robots. The core contribution involves robot control, motion planning, and reinforcement learning for humanoid locomotion and manipulation. The paper explicitly mentions 'deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot' and addresses 'whole-body motions' and 'humanoid control', which are central topics in robotics.

This paper focuses on physical human-robot interaction, proposing a predictive-coding-based mechanism for robot control and behavior regulation during interaction tasks. The core contribution involves developing a variational recurrent neural network architecture for robot decision-making and control during embodied interaction. While the paper uses neural networks and machine learning techniques, the primary application domain and research focus is on robot autonomy, control, and interaction with humans, which are central topics in robotics.

This paper presents a vision-based framework for assessing cognitive workload in human-robot collaborative assembly tasks. The core contribution involves using RGB-D camera observations combined with robot states to interpret operator attention and actions, making it fundamentally a robotics application. While the paper involves computer vision techniques (RGB-D processing), the primary focus is on robot control, human-robot interaction, and collaborative assembly tasks, which are central to robotics research. The paper explicitly addresses 'human-robot collaboration (HRC) in industrial assembly operations' and 'adaptive robot assistance,' positioning it squarely within the robotics domain rather than pure computer vision.

This paper describes the design and experimental validation of a robotic system for medical intervention, specifically for delivering a curved needle-like laser ablator to the hippocampus during epilepsy treatment. The core focus is on robot control, manipulation, and the mechanical design of a robotic system for precise medical delivery. While it involves medical imaging (MRI), the primary contribution is the robotic system design and its performance in needle deployment and positioning.

This paper presents EmbodiedSkills, a framework for orchestrating vision-language-action (VLA) models in robotic systems. The core focus is on robot control, manipulation, and planning - specifically how to coordinate perception, planning, execution, and verification for long-horizon robotic tasks. The paper discusses skill execution, prerequisite checking, outcome verification, and deployment on robotic platforms (RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO). While it involves vision-language models, the primary contribution is the framework for robot agent orchestration and control.

This paper presents GLASS, a GPU-accelerated linear algebra library specifically designed for robotics applications on edge devices. While it involves robotics systems and edge computing, the primary focus is on the software library design, optimization, and performance tuning of numerical computations. The paper emphasizes architecture-specific placement decisions, compiler-time optimization, and software engineering aspects of building reusable numerical infrastructure. Although robotics applications are mentioned as motivation and validation, the core contribution is a software engineering solution for linear algebra computation.

This paper focuses on robot control, trajectory planning, and manipulation for a surgical robot system. The core contribution involves numerical techniques for trajectory smoothing and real-time control of a parallel robot's end-effector, which are fundamental robotics problems. While the application is medical (pancreatic surgery), the primary technical contribution is in robot control and motion planning rather than medical imaging, human-computer interaction, or other domains.

This paper addresses robot planning in unknown environments with movable obstacles, focusing on the decision between navigation and relocation strategies. The core contributions involve robot motion planning, obstacle manipulation, and path planning algorithms. The work is fundamentally about robot control and planning in dynamic environments with perception constraints, which are central topics in robotics.

This paper focuses on robotic manipulation tasks, specifically addressing how Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can be continuously adapted for robot control. The core contribution involves action normalization strategies for robotic systems performing manipulation tasks (single-arm and bimanual). The paper explicitly discusses 'robotic manipulation tasks,' 'robot control,' and 'lifelong VLA adaptation' in the context of physical robot execution, which are central topics in robotics research.

This paper focuses on robot control and manipulation, specifically developing a Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI)-based control framework for robotic manipulators. The core contributions involve real-time dynamics-based control, torque sampling, and force-aware manipulation for compliant robot behavior. The paper explicitly addresses 'robot control, manipulation, locomotion, and planning and perception for robots' which are the defining topics of cs.RO.

This paper presents MR-Robotics LAB, a mixed-reality platform for teaching robotics without physical hardware. The core contribution focuses on robot control, visualization, and manipulation in a virtual environment, with emphasis on 'robot motion', 'joint configurations', 'end-effector grasping', and 'robot trajectory' replay. While the paper has educational (cs.HC) and software engineering (cs.SE) elements, the primary technical contribution centers on robotics simulation and visualization—specifically how robot trajectories are controlled and displayed in mixed reality for educational purposes.

This paper focuses on robot manipulator trajectory planning under kinematic constraints, using inverse kinematics solvers and gradient-based optimization for robot control and motion planning. The core contributions involve differentiable parameterizations for IK solvers and trajectory optimization for robotic manipulation tasks, with hardware demonstrations on a robot arm. The primary subject matter is robot control, planning, and manipulation.

This paper focuses on safety-critical control systems, uncertainty quantification, and control synthesis using adaptive conformal prediction and control barrier functions. The core contribution involves developing a control framework that integrates uncertainty quantification with safety constraints for robotic/autonomous systems control. While the paper uses machine learning techniques (conformal prediction), the primary application domain is control systems and safety assurance, which falls under robotics and autonomous systems control.

This paper focuses on robotic insertion for construction assembly, specifically addressing how to determine appropriate contact forces for robotic manipulation tasks. The core contribution involves robot control, force limits, and manipulation planning for assembly operations. While the paper uses LLMs and finite element analysis as tools, the primary problem domain and application area is robotic manipulation and control for construction assembly tasks.

This paper investigates motion-prior regularization techniques for training diffusion policies on robotic insertion tasks with limited demonstrations. The core focus is on robot control and manipulation (insertion tasks), with experiments conducted on real robots. While the paper involves machine learning (diffusion policies), the primary application domain and research question center on robotic task performance and control strategies.

This paper focuses on vision-language-action (VLA) policies for robot control and manipulation. The core contribution is improving action generation for robotic tasks, with real-world experiments on a Franka Emika Panda robot demonstrating smoother motion and faster task completion. The work addresses robot control, manipulation, and planning/perception for robots, which are central topics in robotics.

The paper focuses on runtime verification for autonomous and robotic systems, specifically presenting a verification pipeline called PREDICTIVE VARANUS. The key application domain mentioned is 'a robotic rover for nuclear-store inspection,' and the abstract emphasizes monitoring behavior during execution of robotic systems. While the paper involves formal methods (CSP, LTL, runtime verification), the primary motivation and application context is robotic systems and their safe autonomous operation.

This paper describes a wearable pneumatic haptic device system for tactile interaction, with applications in teleoperation and human-robot interaction. The core contributions involve hardware design (pneumatic devices with sensing and actuation), human studies evaluating tactile feedback effectiveness, and integration with robotic systems. While it touches on robotics applications (robot gripper mounting, teleoperation), the primary focus is on the haptic interface technology itself, human perception of tactile feedback, and human-computer interaction through touch. The emphasis on user studies, perceptual discrimination, mental workload reduction, and interaction design places this squarely in human-computer interaction territory.

This paper focuses on vision-language-action (VLA) models applied to robotic manipulation tasks, specifically addressing real-world online reinforcement learning for robot control. The core contributions involve improving robot policy learning through RL algorithms (Asymmetric Co-Bootstrapping) and architectural improvements for efficient robot control. The paper explicitly mentions 'robot embodiments', 'manipulation', 'policy improvement', and robot control in real-world settings, which are central topics in robotics research.

This paper focuses on guiding vector fields (GVFs) for robot path following, addressing singularity elimination and speed control. The core contributions involve designing vector fields that guide robot trajectories to desired paths, with applications demonstrated on quadrotor control. The work is fundamentally about robot control, trajectory planning, and path following - all central topics in robotics. While the paper involves mathematical control theory, the primary application domain and motivation are robotic systems.

This paper focuses on camera-to-robot calibration for mobile robots, which is fundamentally about robot perception and control. The core contribution involves calibrating camera pose relative to robot coordinate systems using laser tracking, which is essential for robot manipulation and navigation. The paper explicitly addresses 'camera-equipped mobile robots' and their calibration, which falls squarely within robotics research concerning robot perception and control systems.

This paper focuses on the design, development, and validation of a powered knee prosthesis device, including mechanical engineering aspects (actuator design, transmission optimization, structural analysis), control systems (position and torque control), and experimental validation with human users. The core contribution involves robot control, manipulation, and perception for a robotic prosthetic device, which directly aligns with robotics research. While there are biomechanical elements, the primary emphasis is on the engineering design and control of the prosthetic limb system.

This paper focuses on multi-robot navigation in human-shared spaces, addressing robot control, motion planning, and coordination. The core contributions involve trajectory planning, adaptive replanning based on human responses, and robot team coordination in interactive environments. While it involves prediction of human responses, the primary emphasis is on robot motion planning, control, and navigation strategies rather than human-computer interaction design or language processing.

This paper focuses on filter design and state estimation for autonomous underwater vehicle navigation systems. The core contribution involves developing an Equivariant Filter (EqF) that improves upon existing Kalman filter variants (IEKF, MEKF) by better handling the geometric structure of the navigation state space. The work is fundamentally about estimation algorithms, sensor fusion, and navigation system design rather than robotics control/manipulation, computer vision, or other domains. While AUVs are robotic systems, the paper's primary focus is on the mathematical framework and filtering algorithms for navigation state estimation.

This paper focuses on improving robotic manipulation through vision-language-action (VLA) models by guiding visual attention to task-relevant regions. The core contribution involves training robotic policies to perform high-precision manipulation tasks, with emphasis on robot control, perception, and action prediction. While the paper involves vision and language components, the primary application and evaluation are centered on robotic manipulation and control, which is the defining characteristic of robotics research.

This paper presents World Action Agent (WAA), a system for robot manipulation that uses vision-language models to control robots through visual action workspaces.
